definitions.explanation: Selling goods by traveling from place to place rather than operating from a fixed store. The person who does this is called a {行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}.

examples.japanese: {行商|ぎょうしょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{生計|せいけい}→生計：13524_seikei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧。
examples.english: To make a living by peddling.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{行商|ぎょうしょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{回|まわ}っていた→回る：01150_mawaru⟧。
examples.english: In the old days, fish peddlers would go around town.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、リヤカー⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{引|ひ}いて→引く：01978_hiku⟧⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{行商|ぎょうしょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧そうだ。
examples.english: I heard my grandfather used to peddle vegetables pulling a cart when he was young.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{行|ぎょう}→行：26669_gyou⟧ (travel/go) + ⟦{商|しょう}→商：26727_shou⟧ (commerce/trade). Refers to the practice of selling goods by going from place to place, rather than from a fixed shop.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {行商|ぎょうしょう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to peddle, to sell door-to-door
- {行商|ぎょうしょう}{人|にん}: peddler, traveling salesperson
- {行商|ぎょうしょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: to go out peddling

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{露店|ろてん}→露店：10106_roten⟧: street stall — a temporary booth set up in one place
- {物売|ものう}り: vendor, seller — more general term

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional {行商|ぎょうしょう} was common in Japan before the spread of supermarkets. Fish, tofu, and vegetable peddlers would walk through neighborhoods. While rare today, some traveling vendors still operate in rural areas.
